cards.title: Introduction to Logging
cards.content:
Logging is a crucial part of any Python application. Instead of using print() statements, the built-in logging module provides a flexible framework for emitting log messages from applications.

import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logging.info('Application started')

content.instructions: Order the standard Python log levels from lowest severity to highest severity.

content.text: To set the minimum severity threshold for the root logger, you use logging.______(level=logging.DEBUG).

cards.title: Components of Logging
cards.content:
Advanced logging involves multiple components:

  • Loggers: Expose the interface that application code uses directly.
  • Handlers: Send the log records (created by loggers) to the appropriate destination.
  • Filters: Provide a finer grained facility for determining which log records to output.
  • Formatters: Specify the layout of log records in the final output.

content.instructions: Match each logging component with its correct description.

pairs.right: Exposes the interface for application code
Sends log records to destinations like files or console
Specifies the final layout of the log record
Determines which records to output based on criteria

cards.title: Logging Best Practices
cards.content: Always use the appropriate log level. Do not log sensitive data like passwords or tokens. Use lazy formatting in log messages (e.g., logging.info('User %s logged in', username) instead of f-strings) to save CPU cycles when logging is disabled.
